approach: Redo both fixes from the base, with the missed fixture included. (1) In gh/client.rs, `classify_checks` becomes the one place that reads the check-runs and status replies and returns a `CheckReport { checks, notes }`. It judges only the check run named `CI_AGGREGATE_JOB` ("fmt, clippy, tests"): failed is Red, missing or unfinished is Pending, finished and not failed is Green. Every other failed check run or failed legacy status becomes a note. A new `PrHost::check_report` has a default that wraps `checks` with no notes; `GhClient` overrides it with the existing two reads, and `checks` becomes its `.checks`. `wait_for_checks` and `land_pr` use `check_report` and put the notes of the last read into `PrReport.warnings`. `EARLY_RUN_JOB` refers to `CI_AGGREGATE_JOB`. (2) In invariant.rs, `closing_jobs` skips a job whose tree has `candidate.json` but no verification and no outcome (the shape a held job commits, per CHANGELOG D146), so `classify_pre_merge` calls such a commit records only. A job with an outcome and no verification still returns `NoVerification`. (3) Every test fake that serves a `check_runs` reply names its run 'fmt, clippy, tests': external_calls.rs:90, gh/tests.rs:86 and :2192, and the `done`/`running` helpers at gh/tests.rs:675-680. CHANGELOG and a decision entry record both fixes. No refusal or matching rule changes.

decisions.choice: Return notes with the verdict as `CheckReport { checks, notes }` from `classify_checks`, and add `PrHost::check_report` with a default that wraps `checks()`.
decisions.reason: One read of check runs and status yields both, so there is no extra API call. The default keeps FakeHost, the delegating host near gh/tests.rs:1600 and every other PrHost fake compiling and unchanged.

rejected.option: A separate `optional_failures(commit)` method that reads the host again
rejected.why: That is the rejected earlier design: two extra API calls per look, and notes could disagree with the verdict.
This would force edits to every PrHost fake, including ones outside the listed deliverables.

decisions.choice: Judge by the one check run named `CI_AGGREGATE_JOB`, taking the highest-id run with that name when a re-run left several (as `parse_check_run` does). Legacy combined statuses and all other check runs are optional and only produce notes.
decisions.reason: This is the request: the PR head check is optional and must not fail a PR whose required check is green. A missing required check stays Pending, so an unnamed fake check run would wait forever. That is why the fixtures need the name.

rejected.why: A red status context is not the required check, so it would keep the same bug through another route.

rejected.option: Read the required names from ci.yml or a list
rejected.why: Out of scope. The constant already exists and is one name.

decisions.choice: Define the name once. `CI_AGGREGATE_JOB` becomes `pub(super)` in client.rs and `EARLY_RUN_JOB` is `= super::client::CI_AGGREGATE_JOB`. Test fakes use `EARLY_RUN_JOB` or `CI_AGGREGATE_JOB` within athena-core. The external integration test, a separate crate, cannot reach a private constant, so it uses a literal 'fmt, clippy, tests' with a comment.
decisions.reason: Criterion 7: one definition in non-test code.

rejected.why: That is the duplication being removed.
This widens the public surface for a test-only need; a commented literal in the integration test is smaller.

decisions.choice: The held-job rule goes in `closing_jobs`: a job is not closing when its tree has a candidate, no verification, no `outcome.json` and no later outcome. A new helper `held(&JobFiles)` sits beside `not_landed`.
decisions.reason: `closing_jobs` is the single source for 'this commit lands a job', used by `classify_pre_merge`, `landing` and `land::pr_commits`, so one change covers the PR head check and the landing check. D146 says a held job's records are committed with no score and no outcome. Today `not_landed` is false for a job with no outcome, so a candidate-only commit is wrongly counted as a landing and returns `NoVerification`.

rejected.why: `landing` and `pr_commits` would still disagree about the same commit.

rejected.option: Skip the verification check for any job without an outcome
rejected.why: A finished job's closing records, which carry an outcome, must still need a verification; only the no-outcome shape is exempt.

decisions.choice: Do not change run/mod.rs, land.rs logic, drain.rs or ci.yml. land.rs gets a doc-comment edit only, naming the held-job rule in the `pr_commits` list.
decisions.reason: The earlier candidate did not need run/mod.rs, and drain output is out of scope. The doc edit keeps the comment true.

rejected.option: Surface the notes in drain output

steps: Re-run the search: Grep `check_runs|check-runs` over all *.rs. Confirm the unnamed fakes are exactly external_calls.rs:90, gh/tests.rs:86, :675, :680 and :2192.

In client.rs: make `CI_AGGREGATE_JOB` `pub(super)`; add `pub struct CheckReport { pub checks: Checks, pub notes: Vec<String> }`. Rewrite `classify_checks(runs, status) -> CheckReport` per the decisions: take the highest-id run named `CI_AGGREGATE_JOB`; failed gives Red; missing or not completed gives Pending; otherwise Green. Add a note for every other failed run (an unnamed one is called '(unnamed)') and for a failed legacy status, with the check's name and conclusion and 'not required'. Document it for outside readers.

In client.rs: add to `PrHost` `fn check_report(&self, commit) -> Result<CheckReport>` with a default that wraps `self.checks(commit)` with no notes. In invariant.rs: add `held()` and use it in `closing_jobs` after the `not_landed` check; update docs in invariant.rs and the `pr_commits` doc in land.rs. In landing_tests.rs: add test (a) the held-job commit passes `classify_pre_merge` as records only, and test (b) the finished-job commit with no verification returns `NoVerification`.

risks.risk: Another test fake or fixture returns an unnamed check run and now reads as Pending, which hangs or fails some other test.
risks.mitigation: Step 6 names every fake found by the search (`check_runs` and `check-runs` over all *.rs, and over other file types, which found none). The producer reruns that search after editing, and `cargo test --locked` covers the rest.

risks.risk: Changing `classify_checks` loosens the old Green rule.
risks.mitigation: Keep the same completed-and-not-in-the-failed-set rule as before for the required run. Unit-table cases cover success, skipped, failure and in_progress.

risks.risk: The held-job exemption lets a commit slip through that should need verification.
risks.mitigation: `held` requires a candidate and no verification, no outcome and no later outcome. Test (b) pins the finished-job case. A commit that gets a verification later is a landing at that commit and is judged normally.

risks.risk: Notes repeat across the wait loop's looks.
risks.mitigation: `wait_for_checks` returns the notes of the last read only, and `land_pr` adds them once.

risks.risk: A change to `Checks` or `classify_checks`'s return type breaks a caller outside gh/.
risks.mitigation: The default method `check_report` leaves other implementors untouched, and the compiler flags any missed site.

demonstrations.method: New unit table over `classify_checks` for runs and status JSON: required green with an optional red run gives Green plus one note; required red gives Red; required in_progress gives Pending; no required run (only an optional green run) gives Pending; a failed legacy status with required green gives Green plus a note. With `merge_via_rest` true the report is Landed with the note in `warnings`; with it false the report is Open with `checks == Some(Green)`.
demonstrations.observes: Verdict and notes as listed. Landed or waiting, never failed. The note names the optional check and its conclusion. A required-red reply still gives `checks == Some(Red)`.
